title: The moon as a logical refuge for a space-faring civilization facing catastrophe
summary: Randall Carlson tells of The moon as a logical refuge for a space-faring civilization facing catastrophe, about prehistoric cataclysm cycles at The Moon, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: which could be off planet and to a a civilization with space fairing capabilities. To me, the moon would be the logical place.
And the logical place, and this is even scenarios that have been profered by NASA, is that a logical place for us to create a place of refuge would be the moon.
tellings.difference: Ties the catastrophe to a Younger Dryas–scale comet, credits NASA with similar scenarios, and frames the refuge as one we would build ourselves.
tellings.link_reason: Randall Carlson again calls the moon the logical refuge from a cosmic catastrophe, the same theory he gave in telling 2.

as_told.title: Moon as a refuge from a Younger Dryas–scale comet catastrophe

tellings.quote: Well, the most obvious one would be the moon.
tellings.difference: Ties the refuge explicitly to the Younger Dryas catastrophe.
tellings.link_reason: Carlson again names the moon as the obvious refuge for a civilization fleeing catastrophe.
